47500121.extract:
Banshee (Irish: Bheansidhe) is the fourth collection by British designer Alexander McQueen, released for the Autumn/Winter 1994 season of his eponymous fashion. The collection is deeply rooted in Irish folklore and is a significant part of McQueen's fashion history, inspiring future collections.

Banshee, a female spirit in Irish folklore, is a harbinger of death, often wailing or shrieking to warn of a family member's demise. Alexander McQueen, a renowned British fashion designer, drew inspiration from the mythological figure to create his fourth fashion collection, Banshee.

In Alexander McQueen's second runway show, he drew inspiration from Irish folklore about banshees who were heard wailing when a boat sank. This collection, released for the Autumn/Winter 1994 season, marked a significant moment in his career, showcasing his ability to blend storytelling, history, and raw emotion into his designs. The collection featured intricate patterns, dark tones, and dramatic silhouettes, reflecting the haunting and powerful essence of the banshee.

The banshee is an integral part of the brand's history, with the collection paying homage to the legacy of Lee Alexander McQueen. The inspiration is particularly evident in the Spring Summer 2025 collection, where the banshee theme was woven into the fabric of the collection, inspiring the design of garments, hair, and accessories.

McQueen reinvents the Banshee in a spellbinding campaign
========================================================

Immersed in the Celtic and mythological universe, McQueen's spring-summer 2025 campaign reinvents the banshee, an inspiring and powerful figure, through a breathtaking Welsh landscape.

02.12.2025 by Pauline Borgogno

![Image 9](blob:http://localhost/117fc80ca205ff611ce2b73fe7c7efa4)![Image 10: person advertisement poster book publication clothing dress face head outdoors](https://www.lofficielibiza.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.datocms-assets.com%2F70938%2F1739258369-1739137970-mcqueen-ss25-ad-campaign-image-1.jpg%3Fauto%3Dformat%252Ccompress%26cs%3Dsrgb&w=3840&q=75)

In a reinterpretation of Celtic folklore, [**McQueen**](https://www.lofficielibiza.com/fashion/mcqueen-banshee-spring-summer-2025-show-pfw) ’s Spring/Summer 2025 campaign immerses us in **the dark and fascinating world of the banshee** , a mythological figure that haunts the night and announces death. This mystical entity, which creative director [**Seán McGirr**](https://www.lofficielibiza.com/fashion/alexander-mcqueen-autumn-winter-2024-by-sean-mcgirr) discovered during his childhood in Ireland, becomes the starting point for the designer’s collection, which reinvents this icon as a powerful force of freedom and expression.

Banshee Inspiration

**Seán McGirr** , who is in his second year as **McQueen** ’s creative director, draws on his Irish roots to breathe new life into the banshee, a creature plagued by fear and superstition. _“The banshee was always part of my childhood imagination,”_ he explains. _“It embodies a sense of intense self-expression, something liberating and connecting_ with others.” In this campaign, the banshee becomes **a symbol of freedom and creative power, a renewal of McQueen’s legacy** that draws on myth to transcend tradition.

![Image 12](blob:http://localhost/117fc80ca205ff611ce2b73fe7c7efa4)![Image 13: fashion adult female person woman clothing coat fur face head](https://www.lofficielibiza.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.datocms-assets.com%2F70938%2F1739258370-1739137970-mcqueen-ss25-ad-campaign-image-5.jpg%3Fauto%3Dformat%252Ccompress%26cs%3Dsrgb&w=3840&q=75)

![Image 14](blob:http://localhost/117fc80ca205ff611ce2b73fe7c7efa4)![Image 15: formal wear suit fashion dress person adult female woman male man](https://www.lofficielibiza.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.datocms-assets.com%2F70938%2F1739258383-1739137970-mcqueen-ss25-ad-campaign-image-2.jpg%3Fauto%3Dformat%252Ccompress%26cs%3Dsrgb&w=3840&q=75)

Credits: Courtesy of McQueen

A campaign in Welsh lands

Captured by photographer **Glen Luchford,** the Spring/Summer 2025 campaign is set against the rugged landscapes of Llansteffan Castle in Wales. This location, steeped in history, offers **a striking contrast between the timeless majesty of the clothes and the harshness of the surrounding nature.** At dusk, silhouettes dressed in the collection’s key pieces move through this environment, where land, sea and stone seem to dialogue with **McQueen** ’s creations.

Clothes between delicacy and audacity

The collection’s pieces, with their **juxtaposition of refinement and brutality,** perfectly embody the spirit of the banshee. The opulent, bejeweled hooded coat and the gold jacket with feather lining stand out for their rich detailing and sophisticated aesthetic. These pieces contrast starkly with the hard-packed Welsh landscape, highlighting the collection’s bold palette and accessories. Delicate fabrics, such as spider lace, pleated chiffon and frayed silk organza, bring a lightness that dialogues with the gravity of the surroundings.

A tribute to the House's heritage

Through this campaign, the artistic director pays homage to **the legacy of Lee Alexander McQueen** , particularly to the fall-winter 1994 collection, which also explored the theme of the banshee. This return to the roots is translated by an ingenious mix of classic tailoring and delicate artisanal techniques. The collection is thus part of this **tradition of deconstructing conventions** , where each piece pushes the limits of elegance and tradition.

**McQueen Spring Summer 2025: creating the Banshee Hair**
---------------------------------------------------------

An innovative textile development from inside the McQueen atelier.

![Image 1: McQueen Spring Summer 2025 Banshee Hair coat photographed backstage in Paris. ](https://amq-mcq.dam.kering.com/asset/957d8b4f-a667-4345-a1db-a7943d4c1a14/Original-Ecom/AM866_SS25_SHOW_TIER-2_PRIORITY_4x5_13.jpg)

Discover innovation at the heart of the [Spring Summer 2025 collection](https://www.alexandermcqueen.com/en-ca/ca/w-ss25-collection), animating the mythological figure that inspired it.

The banshee, embedded within the house’s history and the Irish heritage of creative director Seán McGirr, is woven into fabric of the collection, inspiring the intricate techniques used throughout. Echoing its lore is the ‘banshee hair’ embroidery, wisplike and featherlight, embodying the powerful iconography of the figure’s wind-whipped hair, as she stands tall among nature.

_'The banshee is rooted in the history of McQueen, but it's also a story that I grew up with, so feels deeply personal to me - something I remember my mother talking about in Ireland. describing the cry of this solidarity, foreboding figure. For me, she has come to represent something real and potent now. The idea of someone who is feeling and forthright; someone who can be seen as a guiding force.' - Seán McGirr, creative director._

The McQueen atelier drew inspiration from the banshee’s comb, an object embedded in Celtic folk tales, as well as throughout the collection , describing the banshee as combing her hair with a gleaming silver comb.

The process of the ‘banshee hair’ embroidery required innovative textile manipulation, delicately teasing sections of organza with a fine-toothed comb and massaging the fabric by hand. The resulting texture is a tactile hair-like finish _—_ an intricate evocation of the banshee, and the creativity, storytelling and innovation at the heart of McQueen.

In a show that celebrates the heritage of the maison but also the cultural roots of the new creative director **Sean McGirr**, the SS25 collection of McQueen paid homage to **Irish and Scottish folklore**. _“The banshee is an integral part of the brand’s history_,” writes the designer. “_But it’s also a story I grew up with, so for me, it’s extremely personal_.” At the **École des Beaux-Arts**, on a metal runway decorated with cracked tiles—a detail that evokes the eerie sets so loved by McQueen—the brand’s new collection looks to the archives, particularly the **FW94** inspired by the mythical figure of the **banshee**, a female spirit that for McGirr represents _“something powerful and real, someone who can be seen as a guiding force”_. From the McQueen show that served as inspiration, silhouettes and materials could be recognized, including long lace dresses and embroidered English tailoring. With the addition of towering platform shoes, hats and wool skull masks, blood-red details, and taffeta corsets, McGirr demonstrated that he has finally fully immersed himself in the brand's universe and emerged **more aware**. After a first show, FW24, which initially disappointed expectations but later left a mark thanks to impactful accessories like the [hoof shoes](https://www.nssmag.com/it/fashion/37782/sean-mcgirr-debutto-hoof-shoes-alexander-mcqueen), the Irish designer continues to keep the industry's attention, this time grabbing it by the throat with grand classics.

With the first looks gloriously embodying the maison’s typical **tailoring expertise**, a style code owed to Lee McQueen’s past in the **Savile Row** ateliers, the first references to the banshee appear in the feathered tops peeking from the blazers and the ruffles adorning collars and cut-outs. Soon after, the first direct portrayal of the figure appears, a white ruffled dress cinched at the waist with a leather belt. When the model turns her back to the audience, the back of the **wool hat** she wears reveals **the face of a skull**, another nod to the macabre icons beloved by the founder of the maison. Following this, voluminous dresses and hyper-English suits decorated with silver embroidery and bulky collars alternate. **Asymmetry and rigidity** once again draw from the brand’s archive, while new McGirr-signed styles emerge in footwear, with oxford shoes and thick leather boots featuring a tongue held by a large silver buckle. Halfway through the show, bright colors briefly step away from the banshee’s world, with pink, yellow, and orange ruffles swirling alongside sparkling rhinestones. Extremely ordinary pieces debut, adding greater commercial appeal to the collection, such as **beige trench coats, leather jackets and mini skirts**, and **Glen plaid coats**, before returning to the banshee with distressed metallic fringes, a new white wool mask, and a multitude of dresses—some well-structured, others softer—adorned with soft white feathers.

The final looks of the collection speak of a gala banshee, a mystical figure wearing voluminous white dresses but also jackets entirely covered in **buttons, beads, and gold bolts**—perhaps a reference to another famous Lee McQueen collection, the [FW99 Givenchy](https://www.nssmag.com/it/fashion/35537/robot-schiaparelli-cyborg-couture). The designs become more dramatic towards the end, with **thorn-shaped appliqués**(another reference to a past collection, the FW06 that also inspired the look McGirr created for Lana Del Rey at the latest Met Gala)that twist around a model’s torso and a gray silk cloud vaporizing around another model’s legs. The banshee returns to the École des Beaux-Arts in a new form, a **bundle of sparkling rhinestones** twisting from head to toe. Having had more time to create the collection, McGirr explained backstage, it was easier this time to study the brand's archives and delve deeper into its history to revisit it in a modern way. While the fashion industry was outraged by the irony with which the young designer took his first steps as the brand’s creative director in FW24, this time McGirr has shown his **more mature and respectful side**. With the certainty that coats and blazers will sell, the designer can now breathe a sigh of relief; let's just hope he doesn’t get overwhelmed by the desire to please at all costs and retains some of the charming wickedness that left everyone speechless last February.

7.title: McQueen Embraces the Banshee’s Cry for Spring 2025
7.description: For Seán McGirr's second Alexander McQueen collection, the designer dove deep into the archives.
7.content:
FASHION

![Image 1: Model on the runway at Alexander McQueen RTW Spring 2025 as part of Paris Ready to Wear Fashion Week...](https://imgix.bustle.com/uploads/image/2024/9/30/dd610d3f/gettyimages-2174462540.jpg?w=414&h=621&fit=crop&crop=focalpoint&dpr=2&fp-x=0.4874&fp-y=0.1119)

Photo by Giovanni Giannoni/WWD via Getty Images

On Saturday, the still-new Alexander McQueen creative director Seán McGirr presented his second collection on Paris’s left bank. This offering was rooted in a rawly emotional concept: he looked to Lee McQueen’s autumn/winter 1994 show “Banshee,” which opened with two pregnant women walking to the screams of Irish fairy women, mourning a death that is soon to come.

“The banshee is rooted in the history of McQueen, but it’s also a story that I grew up with, so it feels deeply personal to me—something I remember my mother talking about in Ireland, describing the cry of this solitary, foreboding figure,” McGirr explained backstage. This emotive memory, along with McGirr’s own more optimistic interpretation of this mournful, haunting but powerful figure, form the basis of a collection that is both more romantic and beautifully wearable than his debut. “[The banshee] has come to represent something real and potent now,” he says. “The idea of someone who is feeling and forthright; someone who can be seen as a guiding force.”

Photo by Giovanni Giannoni/WWD via Getty Images

Photo by Giovanni Giannoni/WWD via Getty Images

Photo by Giovanni Giannoni/WWD via Getty Images

This came to life with dark, twisted (literally, with fabric contorting) tailoring. The opening looks gave us foreboding and sharply executed suiting and dresses, layered over Elizabethan collared shirting and raw-edge heritage lace. McGirr played with McQueen’s use of the S-bend—the straight-front corset popular in the early 1900s. Constriction took several forms, with houndstooth jackets turning into themselves. A gorgeous silk lemon organza dress was a highlight, striking with the deep romanticism we have come to expect from the house of McQueen, but given lightness. The final look, an otherworldly gown made of silver chains wrapping from the head down the body, packed a visual punch.

6.title: The Banshee, A Folkloric Tale By McQueen - V Magazine
6.content:
In McQueen’s universe, no one is merely a victim or a ghost, they are a force. And as always, a McQueen campaign is more than just fashion

February 7, 2025

Llansteffan Castle looms over the Welsh coastline, enveloped in mist and myth. For the Spring/Summer 2025 campaign, Creative Director Seán McGirr summons the ghostly wail of the banshee, a figure native to Irish folklore. Shot by Glen Luchford, the images capture a cast of characters bound to land, sea, and sky by an unseen, unrelenting force.

![Image 1: A woman in an off-white strapless dress and winged heels lies in tall grass, holding a ball of light in one hand, with the word McQueen printed above her and a large castle ruin in the background, in a black and white image](https://vmagazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/McQueen-SS25-Ad-Campaign-Image-6-scaled.jpg)

Photograph by Glen Luchford

The banshee has long been part of McQueen’s visual lexicon. In his second-ever runway show, Lee Alexander McQueen himself referenced Irish folklore, drawing from tales of wailing spirits said to forewarn of tragedy at sea. Shown at London’s legendary Café de Paris, that early collection strengthened McQueen’s ability to weave storytelling, history, and raw emotion into his designs. Now, decades later, Seán McGirr revisits this folkloric being with a new lens.

![Image 2: A model is showcasing the McQueen brand on a beach, wearing a black, long-sleeved dress with a sheer bodice and a fringed skirt, paired with black sandals](https://vmagazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/McQueen-SS25-Ad-Campaign-Image-8-scaled.jpg)

Photograph by Glen Luchford

“The banshee was a figure that was very present in my childhood imagination growing up in Ireland, and she has recently taken on new meaning for me,” says McGirr. “She embodies a sense of strident self-expression that resonates now—something freeing that drives connection with others.”

For the collection, textures and silhouettes mimic the mythological creature’s spectral presence. Sharp tailoring that dissolves into frayed lace, shredded organza, and sculpted outerwear. The palette shifts between whites, gray, and blacks, enhanced by flickers of gold and ember-like orange.

![Image 3: Five fashion models are dressed in formal wear and standing in a group. The word McQUEEN is written in large white letters across the center](https://vmagazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/McQueen-SS25-Ad-Campaign-Image-2-scaled.jpg)

Photograph by Glen Luchford

Embellishments refine the silhouette, capturing the depth of a folkloric tale. Delicate beading, dimensional jewelry, and intricate embroidery add layers of texture and meaning to the collection.
